label: copy phase (recall_idx>=2): input in {0,y,h,l,2,g,x,i,r,1} while outputting one of {q,m,y,1,x,0,l,g,p,a,h,i}
explanation: Copy-phase-only feature: 99.9% of activation mass is at t > L, almost none at recall_idx 0-1, and it is concentrated at recall_idx >= 3 and near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1 holds ~65% of mass). It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, and does not fire on the first occurrence of a token. Inside the copy phase it acts like a lookup on the (input token, output token) pair: input tokens 0, y, h, l, 2, g, x, i are enriched, and output tokens q, m, y, 1, x, 0 are strongly enriched (rate 10-14% vs a 5% copy-phase baseline). The strongest activations are outputting m or q at the last step, after inputs 0/2/h/l (e.g. x p 0 m, m r h m, ... 0 -> q). The conjunction of the two token sets reaches dev F1 0.43 and mass recall 0.74, but precision is only ~0.31: many pairs from these sets never fire, and some active steps fall outside them. Repeated tokens (in_count/out_count) and digit content add little. Magnitude is higher late in the copy and for the m/q outputs; I did not find any further rule for it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 0, y, h, 2, l, g; least: k, w, v, e) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: q, m, y, 1; delimiter step: 1, h, 2, l; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, t=7, L=8 & t=5.
